## Design

### 2026-10-19 – ### Schematic

**1.5h**

### Schematic

I just read the entire tutorial on how to do everything and it took me about 3 minutes. Really wasn't much.

I got started but the main problem I faced was importing libraries. The Hack Club library took me a bit to import. Not too hard but I got it in.

I added all the components I wanted, things that were cool. I added a bunch of lights because they were daisy-chainable and looked really cool. I added 2 buttons instead of 3. I really wanted to add a mini joystick. I found one from Adafruit and they provided the schematic but I had a lot of trouble getting it into KiCad so I didn't use it. I replaced it with the click from the rotary encoder and another slider.

Anyway the entire schematic is done. Here is the picture of the board schematic and that full thing.

### 2026-10-20 – ### PCBING

**1.15h**

### PCBING

I took a bit of time to play around with the layouts my pieces could go in and eventually settled on one I liked. It took a bit of time but I think it was well worth it.

After that I wanted to make these cool hexagonal capacitive keys, and that was the most time-consuming because I kept messing up. I had to Google a bunch of stuff but I did get it on my first try. The sizing was good so I did have to change it and stuff.

Tomorrow I'm probably going to wire everything up and make sure it's all good and then probably make a case or something for it.

### 2026-10-21 – ### PCB is hard

**2h**

### PCB is hard

This took a really long time. First I tried routing it but after a few minutes I realized that with my current layout and how I was routing it, it wasn't possible. I had to play around with layouts until I got one that I thought was actually possible to route.

I routed it and used the bottom layer for power and ground and the top layer for actual signals. I think that should be good. I then spent a bit of time adding things to it.

It was really really hard to get 3D models and I don't know why. That was a lot of work but I did get them in, added images, artwork, and everything, and got it onto JLC PCB. Here are some images of everything.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/b1e8cec08289548d44f4de25aa6ed8e72a888b859848e573694c8ce77ea229ed.png)

### 2026-10-22 – ### CAD-ING ???

**1.1h**

### CAD-ING ???

I spent a bit of time making a little case for my PCB. I was thinking of adding a little cap but we have capacitive buttons and switches and also a bit of artwork on it. I decided it's not worth it to have a small thing on top so it's fine.

I have a little compartment underneath to make it battery-powered. I can just stick a little charging module in there and hook it up, so it's really simple.

I also made a keycap as you can see. I'm not sure exactly what to put on top of it but it's there.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/72b12f0cac3054ee343d61bc99d8c1fabb034933e920ea177fdb7135929495cf.png)

### 2026-10-23 – ### CODE

**0.7h**

### CODE

I've actually never made anything like this. I've never made something that adds inputs to my computer. I did rely on ChatGPT for a bit but I understood the code.

In the beginning I just hooked up the buttons and the rotary encoder and I understood all that. The capacitive buttons were a different challenge but I did get those working.

After that I made it so that after you click a button, it types itself onto your computer. Little test, and the lights also turn on. That's kind of it. I think it's all going to work so it should be okay. Here's a little sneak peek at the code.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/7303bd6cf49626ce4f7435a5cc6ae45afd92eeb6de23422dd49646dcf4478362.png)
